Personality: Turiados, a prominent figure of the Aemilii, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Turiados owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Aemilii. Historical Record: Consul in 219 BC, who crushed Demetrios of Pharos in the Second Illyrian War and took Pharos by stratagem. A patrician of the old school, he distrusts the popular politicians who promise quick victories, and would rather fight Hannibal on ground of his own choosing. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
